findings.title: Pi author child has no usable mutation authorization path
findings.implication: The role advertises write/edit/bash but the default execute policy asks for every mutator and the child has RPC UI. The child also lacks the approved-permission audit callback. Successful handshake/read capability therefore does not imply author capability.
findings.recommendation: Keep final guard fail-closed; define a parent-issued task-scoped delegated capability with explicit paths/commands, expiry/session/generation, and parent-owned durable audit. Until that contract exists, advertise this child role as read-only/unavailable for authorship.

findings.title: Pi ready state can outlive failed persona initialization
evidence: plugins/ca-pi/tools/src/extension.ts:session_start markReady before loadPersona and combined catch
findings.implication: A persona read failure is stored as bridge degradation after readiness. A later successful bridge refresh can clear that degraded state while persona remains empty, with no persona retry edge.
findings.recommendation: Make persona loading an explicit prerequisite or a durable independent unavailable capability. Ready/governed rendering must depend on the same actual prerequisite vector as prompt construction.

findings.title: Sidebar installs after disposal when metrics promise resolves late
findings.implication: A disposed session can reclaim terminal width and renderer hooks. The source-module probe disposed while metrics was pending, then observed installed=true and columns 140→99 after resolving metrics.
findings.recommendation: Apply the existing footer generation/lease pattern to sidebar installs, checking before and after await and before patching. Disposal invalidates every pending install.

findings.title: Qualified production artifact manifests are rejected by farm parser
findings.implication: Farm accepts exact top-level keys format/version/protocol/schema_version/binaries. Promotion adds context_qualification, and production cold execution requires the current platform in that field. Thus a production-qualified manifest shape fails farm admission before native binary execution. This is current-source incompatibility, not an assertion that a particular published release was observed failing.
findings.recommendation: Use one versioned release-manifest decoder/contract across farm, installers and verification; explicitly admit and validate the supported optional context field. Add an exact qualified-package farm admission test before loosening any trust checks.

findings.title: Farm receipt failure is not a safe author-redispatch instruction
findings.implication: Exit 3 can follow successful task commits/merges and integration worktree cleanup. A new invocation force-resets integration to base and replaces same task branches/worktrees. Reused FARM_RUN_ID also opens an existing run directory and truncates stream evidence.
findings.recommendation: Split recover-receipt from retry-author. Persist an exclusive run identity and durable task/integration commit references, inspect existing refs on recovery, and reproduce missing receipts without scheduling authors. Reject run-ID reuse unless an explicit recovery contract verifies it.

findings.title: Farm gate retry loses containment failure
findings.implication: The executor distinguishes timeout with verified cleanup (124) from unverified cleanup (125/cleanupFailed). runGate reduces all nonzero outcomes to ordinary gate failure, allowing outer author reset/retry; mutation path treats unverified containment as fatal.
findings.recommendation: Return operation result, cancellation reason and containment status as separate typed fields through every caller. Block mutation/reset/retry until prior containment is verified, reusing the mutation path policy where applicable.

findings.title: Farm Git observation failure can appear as no drift
findings.implication: Failed diff/ls-files observations are replaced with empty arrays. Both failures can yield a clean-looking drift result.
findings.recommendation: Use observed-clean/observed-dirty/unavailable states; retry bounded read-only Git probes if appropriate, and stop effects when absence cannot be established.

findings.title: Sandbox dependency cache identity is tied to random checkout basename
findings.implication: Two creates with identical dependency files compute the same hash but random temporary checkout names produce different Docker tags, defeating intended cross-create cache reuse. Current caller also omits the available Nixpacks version component.
findings.recommendation: Build a stable cache key from dependency inputs, supported platform and actual builder/toolchain version. Keep repository name only as a cosmetic label; verify existing image provenance before reuse.

findings.title: Sandbox output overflow kills observation client without stopping workload
findings.implication: Overflow is returned as ordinary exit 1 rather than a distinct interrupted reason. exec stops container only for timeout/abort; probe observed no stop after overflow.
findings.recommendation: Carry overflow as explicit interrupted outcome and run the same verified containment policy as other lost-observation paths. Report stop outcome independently from command failure.

findings.title: Sandbox cleanup and discovery sometimes claim more than observed
findings.implication: Claude-inside error says destroyed after an ignored rm result that may be pre-aborted; create compensation ignores remove results; registry view returns [] when Docker listing fails. destroy/prune already contains a better explicit unknown/re-observe pattern.
findings.recommendation: Reuse destroy/prune observation contracts for create/Claude compensation and registry UI. Keep resource IDs and cleanup unknown until an un-aborted read confirms absence. Propagate cancellation through clone/build and bound helper cleanup.

findings.title: Site search handles loader failure but not query/result-data failure
findings.implication: Pagefind module import has retry state; search/data promises do not. Rejection can preserve stale current-looking results or disable show-all indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Give query and expansion their own error/retry state and finally cleanup, bound to the existing query generation token; retain input and clearly mark old results stale.

findings.title: Private Pi artifact prompt is not general installed Pi approval support
evidence: tools/build-host-packages.py:cold execution synthetic Pi approval evidence
findings.implication: Private entry requires exact Pi 1.0.2 while supported runtime compatibility is 1.1.0. It rejects ordinary agent flows; cold-package workflow reports synthetic-policy-event evidence for Pi. This cannot support a broad claim that all installed Pi artifact approvals are host-observed.
findings.recommendation: Publish a host/capability/evidence-mode matrix from actual admission contracts. Version private approval separately and qualify it on supported Pi before describing it as usable authority; preserve ordinary progress independent of optional attestation.

findings.title: Surface and release build helpers have recoverable partial-write states
findings.implication: Canonical generation is deterministic but many multi-file writes are not atomic; some remove old output before late render/rename failures. This is acceptable only if callers treat failed builds as unusable and rerun from canonical input.
findings.recommendation: Build into a complete fresh staging tree, validate there, then swap an owned output root where practical. Do not expand ordinary file tools into a distributed saga; apply durable receipts primarily to irreversible/external effects.

findings.title: Compatibility metadata validates a removal slogan, not release-history authorization
findings.implication: The literal removalRequires value is shape-checked during surface generation. It does not enforce elapsed releases, version floors, release publication status or actual command removal.
findings.recommendation: Keep provenance-aware removal gate separate and authoritative; generate compatibility prose from that enforceable contract instead of implying this registry literal proves removal eligibility.

findings.title: Claude and Codex promotion intentionally differ but share unknown-outcome recovery
findings.implication: Both pin immutable distribution commits, refuse same-version drift, lease channel writes and read back. Codex requires prior immutable tag before channel advance and rejects malformed current version; Claude combines tag/channel flow and skips downgrade comparison if prior version cannot be read.
findings.recommendation: Preserve host distribution differences. Share verified-ref outcome types and explicitly reject unknown current-channel version if monotonicity is required; provide fresh-work re-observation after any uncertain push rather than blind retry.

findings.title: Site drawer reconnect cleanup may duplicate local handlers
findings.implication: Cleanup removes document Escape handler and resets initialized marker but does not remove local opener/close/tray handlers; reconnecting the same element can bind duplicate toggles.
findings.recommendation: Own all listeners with one AbortController per connection, or retain the once-bound marker while reattaching document listeners. Add one connect-disconnect-reconnect behavior check only if this lifecycle is supported.
